rateBook.title: Seasonal rate book
rateBook.subtitle: NET rates — what Luminous receives
rateBook.resetDone: Restored every band to the client-validated values and recalculated.
rateBook.subtitleLong: Luminous' own MIN / BASE / MAX NET rates by season and room category. This is validated business data — the pricing engine anchors on it rather than modelling seasonality itself.
rateBook.statement: These MIN/BASE/MAX figures are NET rates supplied by Luminous and validated by real operation. They already encode seasonality, so the pricing engine selects a band by season rather than multiplying a seasonality factor on top.
rateBook.editedCount: {count, number} band(s) edited from the client values
rateBook.resetDisabled: Nothing to restore — every band matches the client-validated values.
rateBook.resetEnabled: Restore all 15 bands to the values Luminous supplied.

events.subtitleLong: Known exceptional-demand dates. Events are curated by you, not scraped — a wrong event moves real money, so a human decides what counts.

market.title: Market evidence
market.willNotInfluence: This will be shown but will not move rates.
market.uninterpretable: A price you cannot interpret is not evidence.
market.subtitle: Competitor rates and how much they can be trusted. Only observations you can interpret — known basis, category and stay date — are allowed to move a recommended NET rate.
market.uninterpretableBody: The same number can be a refundable OTA sell price including taxes for a 3-night stay, or a one-night NET rate — only one is comparable to a Luminous NET rate. Confidence is derived from the metadata you supply, and LOW-confidence observations never move a rate.
market.basisNote: The more basis you can state, the higher the confidence — and only you can state it.

history.subtitle: Every accept and override the operator has made, with the system's recommendation alongside it. This record is what will eventually tell us where the engine is wrong.

settings.title: Dynamic rules
settings.previewFailed: Could not price a preview for this configuration.
settings.subtitle: The experimental layer that sits on top of the validated rate book: pace, pickup, events and market. None of these values has been validated with Luminous.
settings.paceDesc: The primary demand signal: on-the-books occupancy versus what the booking curve expects for this lead time. Thresholds are gaps in fractions (0.20 = 20 percentage points).
settings.pickupDesc: Booking acceleration over the recent window — deliberately a smaller lever than pace, because the two must not double-count the same demand.
settings.eventsDesc: Applied only on dates you have flagged in the demand calendar. Normal seasonality is already in the rate book.
settings.marketDesc: Only observations at or above the confidence bar can move a rate. Generic web prices are LOW confidence and are shown but never applied.
settings.rateBookNoticeTitle: Seasonal MIN / BASE / MAX rates are not on this page
settings.rateBookNoticeBody: Those are client-validated business data and live in the Rate Book. Everything here is an unvalidated experiment layered on top, and is always clamped back inside the validated band.
settings.previewNote: A sample stay date priced with your unsaved changes.
settings.unvalidatedBody: Pace thresholds, pickup sensitivity, event impact sizes and market sensitivity were all chosen by the engineering team. They are listed in ASSUMPTIONS.md and need operator validation. The booking curve behind pace position is demo data, not Luminous history.
settings.dowDescription: OFF by default. Luminous' rate table shows no weekday structure, so there is nothing to justify a weekday adjustment yet.
settings.boundsDescription: A hard limit on the whole dynamic layer, applied before the validated band clamp.

dataSettings.subtitle: Where your numbers come from.
dataSettings.shadowBody: Prices are recommendations only. Nothing is sent to Blue Jay or any OTA — you apply what you accept, yourself.
dataSettings.unvalidatedBody: Your seasonal NET rates came from you and are treated as fact. Everything layered on top — booking pace thresholds, event impact sizes, market sensitivity — was chosen by the engineering team and still needs your judgement. The booking curve behind pace is demo data, not your history.
